title: [YouPass Collect] - Employment patterns in New Zealand: 1993 & 2003

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The table compares the proportions of male and female workers across six employment sectors in New Zealand in 1993 and 2003.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, men dominated the majority of sectors throughout the period, particularly in IT, farming and building. However, all industries witnessed a narrowing gender gap over the given timeframe.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Starting with the sectors where men were heavily represented, IT had the highest proportion of male employees, at 80% in 1993, followed by farming and building, at 75% and 68%, respectively. By 2003, these figures had all declined to 70%, 65% and 60%, in that order. Conversely, female representation in these three industries saw corresponding increases, with women in IT rising from 20% to 30%, while their counterparts in farming and building grew from 25% and 32% to 35% and 40%, respectively.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to the remaining industries, manufacturing showed a relatively balanced gender distribution, with men accounting for 55% in 1993, which decreased marginally to 52%, while women's share rose from 45% to 48%. In contrast, the service sector was heavily female-dominated at 86% initially, but this figure fell significantly to 60% as male participation surged from just 14% to 40%. Finally, commerce shifted from being slightly female-dominated at 55% to achieving complete gender parity at 50% each in 2003.
